summary: The note profiles Alice Johnson, a 32-year-old literature graduate and writer who became a software developer at InnoTech Solutions after attending a 'Coding for Everyone' workshop in September 2023. It follows her doubts, her mentorship under Michael Zhang, and how her storytelling background improved user-centric product work. It broadens into a call for inclusive education, community networks and a tech industry open to varied backgrounds.
one_line: Literature graduate Alice Johnson's path into software development at InnoTech Solutions illustrates how mentorship, education and community can break tech stereotypes.
key_facts: Alice Johnson is a 32-year-old software developer at InnoTech Solutions.
Alice Johnson holds a bachelor's degree in Literature and was a writer before moving into tech.
Her journey began on September 12, 2023, when she found a coding workshop flyer in a local library.
She attended the 'Coding for Everyone' workshop, wanting to understand coding and maybe build a website for her budding online bookstore.
On September 15, 2023, Alice sat in the seminar room feeling out of place, but held on to small victories each time she solved a problem.
Michael Zhang, a seasoned software engineer and advocate for diversity in tech, became Alice's mentor.
Alice said Zhang helped her see her unconventional background as 'an asset, not a liability'.
On November 20, 2023, Zhang encouraged Alice to apply for an internship at InnoTech Solutions.
Emma Lopez, a product manager, said Alice's way of talking about user stories is 'almost poetic' and helps make products more human-centric.
Alice has been a driving force behind several innovative projects that combine storytelling with user experience.
On December 5, 2023, Alice attended a networking event for non-traditional tech enthusiasts, meeting an ex-chef, a retired professional athlete and a former nurse.
The note says coding bootcamps and online courses are helping chip away at stereotypes and build bridges into tech.
